### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.ai

### Question

The goal is to press `<motion>iF` to select an *empty function body* in lua on top of `nvim-treesitter-textobjects` queries.

```lua
function fn1() end
--            ^ @function.inner

function fn2()
  -- Comments are not part of the body
end
```

```lua
local MiniAi = require("mini.ai")
MiniAi.setup({
  custom_textobjects = {
    F = MiniAi.gen_spec.treesitter({ a = "@function.outer", i = "@function.inner" }),
  },
})
```

Basically:

```lua
|function fn()
  -- Comment
end
```

```
+ ciF =
```

```lua
function fn()|end
```


The problem is that in the lua treesitter grammar there is no `body` node until there is at least one non comment node. An empty function does not even have nodes to select. `#offset` can cut `end`, but there is no way to match the position right after `function(args)`. ¿ So it looks like this can not be solved with a treesitter query alone ?

One possible approach is to refine the region:

1. Get `@function.outer`.
2. Narrow the region.

    2.1. By using patterns:
    
    ```lua
    F = ts_pattern("@function.outer", {
      "^.-function%s*%w+%s*%b()().-()end$",
      --                   ^ relies on %b :(
    })
    ```

    There is no simple way to run `find_textobject` only inside the covered range. `reference_region` seems to work more like exclusion when it is fully defined. So pattern logic would have to be re implemented.

    2.2. Or by selecting between treesitter nodes: `)` and `end`.

Is there a way to solve this with treesitter queries? Or is there a simpler way to approach this problem? I want to find the right direction to take.

🥺 Thanks.

comment_data.body:
> The goal is to press `<motion>iF` to select an _empty function body_ in lua on top of `nvim-treesitter-textobjects` queries.

I am afraid this task is already doomed if taken at face value. The problem is that Neovim has no way to "select nothing", meaning Visual mode selection should always be at least one cell.

There is a [hack for selected cases](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/9990c41f10f54f29a888d13024c9f765037bde23/lua/mini/ai.lua#L1102-L1109) that makes "empty selection" work by [adding single space and acting on it](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/9990c41f10f54f29a888d13024c9f765037bde23/lua/mini/ai.lua#L1136-L1142). This is the only way I know that makes it work. I am pretty sure @TheLeoP and I looked into reasonable ways of making it work with tree-sitter, but I can't remember details (the conclusion was "can't do").

I am going to close this for now, but maybe @TheLeoP can help you more here.

comment_data.body: There is no way to do this while only relying on `nvim-treesitter-textobjects` queries. For example, their query for `@function.outer` in Lua is ```lisp [ (function_declaration) (function_definition) ] @function.outer ``` which, used in the following code ```lua function some_function() end ``` captures the following text defined by the treesitter node ```lisp (function_declaration ; [0, 0] - [0, 28] name: (identifier) ; [0, 9] - [0, 22] parameters: (parameters)) ``` So, we know where the range that defines the `@function.outer` capture starts and ends, but we don't know anything about `@function.inner`. --- `nvim-treesitter-textobjects` queries for `@function.inner` are ```lisp (function_declaration body: (_) @function.inner) (function_definition body: (_) @function.inner) ``` and the following code ```lua function some_function() -- some comment end ``` is parsed as ```lisp (chunk ; [0, 0] - [3, 0] (function_declaration ; [0, 0] - [2, 3] name: (identifier) ; [0, 9] - [0, 22] parameters: (parameters) ; [0, 22] - [0, 24] (comment ; [1, 4] - [1, 19] content: (comment_content)))) ; [1, 6] - [1, 19] ``` which does not have a `body:` field inside of the `function_declaration` node. So, nothing matches. If you simply want to match functions that have any node (including a comment) inside them, you can create the file `~/.config/nvim/queries/lua/textobjects.scm` with the following content (don't forget the `; extends` on the first line, you can read `:h treesitter-query-modeline-extends` to learn what it does, but it is required) ```lisp ; extends (function_declaration (_)+ @function.inner) (function_definition (_)+ @function.inner) ``` This would match a lua function with only a comment inside of it, but won't match an empty Lua function. --- Currently, Neovim core, `nvim-treesitter` and `mini.nvim` follow a convention where you can define ranges that span multiple treesitter nodes by using the same capture (e.g. `@function.outer`) on multiple nodes and the resulting range would span the region defined by the start of the first node and the end of the last node. This is what I used in the previous query to define a range using multiple nodes instead of just one (`(_)+ @function.inner`). Matching an empty function (in this case, a Lua function, but this would work for any language) would require a new convention for defining ranges between multiple nodes that starts with the **end** of the first node and ends with the **start** of the last node. This would mean adding new code to `mini.ai` (and `mini.surround`) to create these ranges, requiring new queries and being the only plugin that uses this new convention. You can use your own `MiniAi.gen_spec.treesitter()` in your config that behaves just like the builtin one, but also takes into account this new behavior (you would also need to create your own treesitter queries). An example query would be something like ```lisp (function_declaration (parameters) @function.inner_special "end" @function.inner_special) ``` which, for the following Lua code ```lua function some_function() end ``` will capture the ranges defined by the nodes ```lisp (chunk ; [0, 0] - [1, 0] (function_declaration ; [0, 0] - [0, 28] "function" ; [0, 0] - [0, 8] name: (identifier) ; [0, 9] - [0, 22] parameters: (parameters ; [0, 22] - [0, 24] "(" ; [0, 22] - [0, 23] ")") ; [0, 23] - [0, 24] "end")) ; [0, 25] - [0, 28] ``` and then you can use the end of the `parameter` node (`[0, 24]`) and the start of the `"end"` node (`[0, 25]`) to define the range for the `inner function` textobject for an empty function
comment_data.bodyHTML:
There is no way to do this while only relying on nvim-treesitter-textobjects queries. For example, their query for @function.outer in Lua is

[
  (function_declaration)
  (function_definition)
] @function.outer

which, used in the following code

function some_function() end

captures the following text

defined by the treesitter node

(function_declaration ; [0, 0] - [0, 28]
    name: (identifier) ; [0, 9] - [0, 22]
    parameters: (parameters))

So, we know where the range that defines the @function.outer capture starts and ends, but we don't know anything about @function.inner.

nvim-treesitter-textobjects queries for @function.inner are

(function_declaration
  body: (_) @function.inner)

(function_definition
  body: (_) @function.inner)

and the following code

function some_function()
    -- some comment
end

is parsed as

(chunk ; [0, 0] - [3, 0]
  (function_declaration ; [0, 0] - [2, 3]
    name: (identifier) ; [0, 9] - [0, 22]
    parameters: (parameters) ; [0, 22] - [0, 24]
    (comment ; [1, 4] - [1, 19]
      content: (comment_content)))) ; [1, 6] - [1, 19]

which does not have a body: field inside of the function_declaration node. So, nothing matches. If you simply want to match functions that have any node (including a comment) inside them, you can create the file ~/.config/nvim/queries/lua/textobjects.scm with the following content (don't forget the ; extends on the first line, you can read :h treesitter-query-modeline-extends to learn what it does, but it is required)

; extends

(function_declaration
  (_)+ @function.inner)

(function_definition
  (_)+ @function.inner)

This would match a lua function with only a comment inside of it, but won't match an empty Lua function.

Currently, Neovim core, nvim-treesitter and mini.nvim follow a convention where you can define ranges that span multiple treesitter nodes by using the same capture (e.g. @function.outer) on multiple nodes and the resulting range would span the region defined by the start of the first node and the end of the last node. This is what I used in the previous query to define a range using multiple nodes instead of just one ((_)+ @function.inner).

Matching an empty function (in this case, a Lua function, but this would work for any language) would require a new convention for defining ranges between multiple nodes that starts with the end of the first node and ends with the start of the last node. This would mean adding new code to mini.ai (and mini.surround) to create these ranges, requiring new queries and being the only plugin that uses this new convention. You can use your own MiniAi.gen_spec.treesitter() in your config that behaves just like the builtin one, but also takes into account this new behavior (you would also need to create your own treesitter queries).

An example query would be something like

(function_declaration
  (parameters) @function.inner_special
  "end" @function.inner_special)

which, for the following Lua code

function some_function() end

will capture the ranges

defined by the nodes

(chunk ; [0, 0] - [1, 0]
  (function_declaration ; [0, 0] - [0, 28]
    "function" ; [0, 0] - [0, 8]
    name: (identifier) ; [0, 9] - [0, 22]
    parameters: (parameters ; [0, 22] - [0, 24]
      "(" ; [0, 22] - [0, 23]
      ")") ; [0, 23] - [0, 24]
    "end")) ; [0, 25] - [0, 28]

and then you can use the end of the parameter node ([0, 24]) and the start of the "end" node ([0, 25]) to define the range for the inner function textobject for an empty function

reply_data.body:
`#make-range!` used to be a directive provided by `nvim-treesitter` that is no longer supported. It worked by mocking treesitter nodes with the provided range (which was possible because they owned the code that parsed each node's metadata), but it was really frail and error prone.

You can create a custom directive that modifies the range of a captured treesitter node, but you can't create your own fake nodes. So, you may be able to get something working, but then you'll be back to having to maintain your own set of special queries that make use of your custom directive.

comment_data.body:
### Pattern within treesitter match

A simple approach is to apply a pattern on top of the `@function.outer` capture.

The current implementation is so low-key sus (bad) that I won't "Show and Tell" it in a separate discussion.

The `local find_textobject` function overrides `MiniAi.gen_spec.custom_textobjects` so the specification can be used directly instead of an id.

To reuse `mini.ai` pattern system while treating `^` and `$` as boundaries of the treesitter match region rather than line boundaries, a temporary scratch buffer is used.

Since `mini.ai` appends a newline `\n` after every string, end-of-match patterns need to use `\n$` to work correctly.

As a side note, for this particular implementation, an API like `MiniAi.find_string_textobject(str, ai_type, id|spec, opts)` would be helpful.

### Code

```lua
-- after/ftplugin/lua.lua

vim.b.miniai_config = {
  custom_textobjects = {
    F = vim.g.miniai_ts_pattern({
      a = { cap = "@function.outer" },
      i = {
        cap = "@function.outer",
        pat = {
          { "^.-%b()%s*()%S.-()%s*end\n$", "^.-%b()()%s+()end\n$" },
        },
      },
    }, { n_lines = 500 }),
  },
}
```

<details open><summary>Click me</summary>

```lua
vim.g.miniai_ts_pattern = function(ai_specs, opts_override)
  local MiniAi = require("mini.ai")
  ai_specs = vim.tbl_deep_extend("keep", ai_specs, {
    a = { cap = "@", pat = nil },
    i = { cap = "@", pat = nil },
  })

  local find_textobject = function(spec, ai_type, opts)
    local tmp_id = "_"
    local tmp_restore = MiniAi.config.custom_textobjects[tmp_id]
    MiniAi.config.custom_textobjects[tmp_id] = spec
    local reg = MiniAi.find_textobject(ai_type, tmp_id, opts)
    MiniAi.config.custom_textobjects[tmp_id] = tmp_restore
    return reg
  end

  local joinpos = function(abs_pos, rel_pos)
    return {
      line = abs_pos.line + rel_pos.line - 1,
      col = rel_pos.line == 1 and abs_pos.col + rel_pos.col - 1 or rel_pos.col,
    }
  end
  local match_buf = -1 -- Lazily created
  local match_pattern = function(ref_reg, ai_type, pattern)
    local from, to = ref_reg.from, ref_reg.to
    local buf_text = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_text(0, from.line - 1, from.col - 1, to.line - 1, to.col, {})
    if not vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(match_buf) then
      match_buf = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
    end
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(match_buf, 0, -1, true, buf_text)
    local reg = vim.api.nvim_buf_call(match_buf, function()
      return find_textobject(pattern, ai_type, {
        reference_region = { from = { line = 1, col = 1 } },
        n_lines = #buf_text,
        n_times = 1,
        search_method = "cover_or_next",
      })
    end)
    if reg and reg.from and reg.to then
      return { from = joinpos(from, reg.from), to = joinpos(from, reg.to) }
    end
    return nil
  end

  local ts_spec = MiniAi.gen_spec.treesitter({ a = ai_specs.a.cap, i = ai_specs.i.cap })
  return function(ai_type, id, opts)
    opts = vim.tbl_extend("force", opts or {}, opts_override or {})
    local cap_reg = find_textobject(ts_spec, ai_type, opts)
    if not cap_reg then
      return
    end
    local pat = ai_specs[ai_type].pat
    if not pat or vim.tbl_isempty(pat) then
      return cap_reg
    end
    local pat_reg = match_pattern(cap_reg, ai_type, pat)
    if pat_reg then
      return pat_reg
    end
    opts.n_times = opts.n_times + 1
    return MiniAi.find_textobject(ai_type, id, opts)
  end
end
```

</details>

Pattern within treesitter match

A simple approach is to apply a pattern on top of the @function.outer capture.

The current implementation is so low-key sus (bad) that I won't "Show and Tell" it in a separate discussion.

The local find_textobject function overrides MiniAi.gen_spec.custom_textobjects so the specification can be used directly instead of an id.

To reuse mini.ai pattern system while treating ^ and $ as boundaries of the treesitter match region rather than line boundaries, a temporary scratch buffer is used.

Since mini.ai appends a newline \n after every string, end-of-match patterns need to use \n$ to work correctly.

As a side note, for this particular implementation, an API like MiniAi.find_string_textobject(str, ai_type, id|spec, opts) would be helpful.

Code

-- after/ftplugin/lua.lua

vim.g.miniai_ts_pattern = function(ai_specs, opts_override)
  local MiniAi = require("mini.ai")
  ai_specs = vim.tbl_deep_extend("keep", ai_specs, {
    a = { cap = "@", pat = nil },
    i = { cap = "@", pat = nil },
  })

  local find_textobject = function(spec, ai_type, opts)
    local tmp_id = "_"
    local tmp_restore = MiniAi.config.custom_textobjects[tmp_id]
    MiniAi.config.custom_textobjects[tmp_id] = spec
    local reg = MiniAi.find_textobject(ai_type, tmp_id, opts)
    MiniAi.config.custom_textobjects[tmp_id] = tmp_restore
    return reg
  end

  local joinpos = function(abs_pos, rel_pos)
    return {
      line = abs_pos.line + rel_pos.line - 1,
      col = rel_pos.line == 1 and abs_pos.col + rel_pos.col - 1 or rel_pos.col,
    }
  end
  local match_buf = -1 -- Lazily created
  local match_pattern = function(ref_reg, ai_type, pattern)
    local from, to = ref_reg.from, ref_reg.to
    local buf_text = vim.api.nvim_buf_get_text(0, from.line - 1, from.col - 1, to.line - 1, to.col, {})
    if not vim.api.nvim_buf_is_valid(match_buf) then
      match_buf = vim.api.nvim_create_buf(false, true)
    end
    vim.api.nvim_buf_set_lines(match_buf, 0, -1, true, buf_text)
    local reg = vim.api.nvim_buf_call(match_buf, function()
      return find_textobject(pattern, ai_type, {
        reference_region = { from = { line = 1, col = 1 } },
        n_lines = #buf_text,
        n_times = 1,
        search_method = "cover_or_next",
      })
    end)
    if reg and reg.from and reg.to then
      return { from = joinpos(from, reg.from), to = joinpos(from, reg.to) }
    end
    return nil
  end

  local ts_spec = MiniAi.gen_spec.treesitter({ a = ai_specs.a.cap, i = ai_specs.i.cap })
  return function(ai_type, id, opts)
    opts = vim.tbl_extend("force", opts or {}, opts_override or {})
    local cap_reg = find_textobject(ts_spec, ai_type, opts)
    if not cap_reg then
      return
    end
    local pat = ai_specs[ai_type].pat
    if not pat or vim.tbl_isempty(pat) then
      return cap_reg
    end
    local pat_reg = match_pattern(cap_reg, ai_type, pat)
    if pat_reg then
      return pat_reg
    end
    opts.n_times = opts.n_times + 1
    return MiniAi.find_textobject(ai_type, id, opts)
  end
end
comment_data.bodyText:
Pattern within treesitter match
A simple approach is to apply a pattern on top of the @function.outer capture.
The current implementation is so low-key sus (bad) that I won't "Show and Tell" it in a separate discussion.
The local find_textobject function overrides MiniAi.gen_spec.custom_textobjects so the specification can be used directly instead of an id.
To reuse mini.ai pattern system while treating ^ and $ as boundaries of the treesitter match region rather than line boundaries, a temporary scratch buffer is used.
Since mini.ai appends a newline \n after every string, end-of-match patterns need to use \n$ to work correctly.
As a side note, for this particular implementation, an API like MiniAi.find_string_textobject(str, ai_type, id|spec, opts) would be helpful.
